title: Interest: saving and borrowing
examples: What is the difference between simple and compound interest?
How do I calculate the total cost of a loan?
What does APR actually mean for me?

explain.say: Today we are learning about interest when saving and borrowing money.

items: Interest is the cost of borrowing money.
It is also the reward for saving money.

explain.say: Simple interest is calculated only on the original amount borrowed or saved.
For example, if you save one hundred pounds at five percent simple interest for two years.
Compound interest is calculated on the original amount plus any accumulated interest.
For instance, if you save one hundred pounds at five percent compound interest for two years.
The Annual Percentage Rate or APR shows the true cost of borrowing.

faq.q: What is the main difference between simple and compound interest?
faq.a: Simple interest only uses the starting amount for calculation each time. Compound interest uses the growing total, including previous interest, for the next calculation.
asks: Does compound interest always mean more money?
How does interest build up over time?

faq.q: Why is APR important when I take out a loan?
faq.a: APR gives you one single number to compare the total cost of different loans. It helps you see all the fees included in the interest rate.
asks: What does APR really mean for my pocket?
Should I worry about the APR number?

faq.q: If I save money, do I want simple or compound interest?
faq.a: When saving, you generally want compound interest because it means your money earns money on itself. This helps your savings grow faster.
asks: Which interest type helps me save more?
Is compounding always good for savers?

faq.q: Can I calculate the interest myself?
faq.a: Yes, you can use the basic formulas for both types of interest. Understanding these formulas helps you compare offers accurately.
asks: What formula do I use for interest?
How do I estimate my future savings?

faq.q: Does the time period affect the interest calculation?
faq.a: Absolutely, the longer the time period, the more interest you will earn or pay. This is especially true with compounding.
asks: How long does it take to see big interest?

facts: Interest is essentially the price paid for using someone else's money.
Compound interest is often described as 'interest on interest'.
APR is a standardized way to show the total cost of borrowing.
The longer the compounding period, the higher the total interest paid or earned.

quiz.say: If you borrow £100 at 10 percent simple interest for two years, the total interest paid is:
quiz.why: Simple interest only calculates interest on the original £100 each year, so 10 percent of 100 is 10 pounds, times two years is 20 pounds.

wrong.0: This is wrong because it incorrectly adds the interest from the second year to the principal.
wrong.1: This is wrong because it only calculates the interest for a single year, ignoring the second year.
wrong.2: This is wrong because it multiplies the principal by the rate and time incorrectly.

quiz.say: Which type of interest results in a larger total amount over many years?
quiz.why: Compound interest is superior for growth because the interest itself starts earning interest, leading to exponential growth.

wrong.1: This is wrong because it only uses the initial amount, missing the growth from previous interest payments.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the principal only represents the starting amount, not the total accumulated value.
wrong.3: This is wrong because APR is a measure of cost, not the final accumulated amount.

quiz.say: When comparing two loans, you should focus most on:
quiz.why: The APR is the best tool because it standardizes the cost by including all fees and the interest rate in one figure.

wrong.1: This is wrong because the stated rate often ignores extra fees that increase the true cost.
wrong.2: This is wrong because while term length matters, it doesn't tell you the true cost per year.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the deposit is what you put in, not the cost of borrowing money.
